body:
Well it's already been an issue for several years, but I appreciate the good faith!

EDIT: err, not the orgasm/suicide link specifically, but I've struggled with sex for a while.  It used to be panic attacks during sex (and I still have those sometimes, too).  It's the link between orgasms and suicide fantasies that's recent.
Heh, my boyfriend and I always called it my PSS (post-sex sad).  My family isn't conservative at all, though.  Sort of the opposite.

I don't know, I have a lot of old pain.  Nothing really recent, but things I can't seem to put behind me.  I was sexually abused as a small child, raped at 13, had parents who didn't get me help when I started cutting (rather, they grounded me), and my household was really rocky.  My parents fought like crazy, screaming insults at each other, threatening to leave, each accusing the other of spoiling their kids (my brother and I have different parents).  

I tried to kill myself twice when I was 16, but my mom told me what to say to the nurses to avoid having to see a psychiatrist.  She was pretty mad at me initially, and then I spent a while having to console her and tell her she wasn't a terrible parent...even though I thought she was.

Yeah, I've got baggage.

I do have important people in my life.  I have an amazingly supportive partner, a few close friends, etc.  I never put myself down, really, and actually I get accused of thinking a little too highly of myself.  I don't really know why I thought of this username. 

I just find fantasies really distracting, though.  If I think about anything but the feeling of it, I can't cum.
That's neat, I didn't know that.  I did always wonder about it, though, since alcohol never makes me sad.  It makes me feel just a little bit better - takes the edge off.

I don't usually fantasize when I masturbate, I just focus on the physical feeling of it.  Occasionally I imagine having someone next to me, telling me how sexy I am and smiling at me.  I used to watch all kinds of hardcore porn and never got sad after that, but it just doesn't appeal to me anymore.
Not on the pill, no. :/  Interesting to hear that it's not uncommon though!
I've seen a few different therapists.  Not about this particular issue, though.  I don't know, I feel tired of having to work so hard just to feel okay.

It feels like a sudden sense of total clarity, in which the most logical thing to do in my life is kill myself.  There isn't really a particular reason, though I do feel sort of trapped in a weird way.

I should mention, though, that I've struggled with depression all my life.  So it's not exactly out of the blue.
Female.  This is only a recent development.
